/help/calendly-and-cal-com.title: Turning Calendly and Cal.com bookings into leads ⋅ Billow
/help/calendly-and-cal-com.description: How to connect a Calendly or Cal.com account, choose the event types that count and turn pending bookings into leads from the board or the list, what Billow suggests for each booking, and what cancellations, reschedules and disconnecting change.
h1: Turning Calendly and Cal.com bookings into leads
h2: Create a lead from a booking
Access follows the person who connected
h3: Turning a lead into a project
p: Turning Calendly and Cal.com bookings into leads

How to connect a Calendly or Cal.com account, choose the event types that count and turn pending bookings into leads from the board or the list, what Billow suggests for each booking, and what cancellations, reschedules and disconnecting change.

You can connect a Calendly or Cal.com account to your workspace so that calls booked with you arrive in your lead pipeline. Only owners and admins can connect an account, and the integration is included on the Grow and Scale plans, along with the rest of the pipeline.
Under Provider, choose Calendly or Cal.com.
Paste your Calendly personal access token or your Cal.com API key. The link under the field opens the page in Calendly or Cal.com where you create one.

Billow confirms with “Calendly connected” or “Cal.com connected”, and the account appears in the list below. The token can’t be viewed or changed after connecting. To use a different token, disconnect the account and connect it again.
The Integrations tab only appears for owners and admins.
A new connection has no event types checked, so no booking creates a lead until you choose some.
Click the arrow next to the account to show its event types. A new connection shows them already.
Check each event type that should create leads.
Billow confirms with “Event types saved”. Bookings on event types you leave unchecked are ignored. Unchecking an event type doesn’t change the leads it already created.

The list is loaded from Calendly or Cal.com each time you open the page. Calendly lists only its active event types. An event type you checked stays checked when Calendly or Cal.com stops listing it, for example because you paused it, until you uncheck it. If Billow can’t reach the provider, it keeps your saved selection and shows “Couldn’t load the current event types.” followed by the reason.
You can connect any number of Calendly and Cal.com accounts, for example your own and a partner’s. Each one has its own row and its own event types.
Each account can only be connected to a workspace once. Connecting it a second time fails with “This Calendly account is already connected.” or “This Cal.com account is already connected.”

Each connected account appears as a row under Settings → Integrations. The row shows the provider, the account’s name and email, how many event types create leads, who connected it, and when the last booking was received, or “No bookings yet”.
Leads that Billow creates on its own are created in the name of the person who connected the account.
“Calendly did not accept this token. Check that it is copied in full and still active.”
The token is wrong, incomplete or revoked. Cal.com shows the same message for its API key.
“Calendly webhooks need a paid Calendly plan (Standard or higher).”
Your Calendly account is on the free plan, which can’t send bookings to Billow.
“Calendly could not be reached. Try again in a moment.”
Calendly or Cal.com rejected the request, followed by its own reason.
When someone books one of your checked event types, Billow looks for a contact with the invitee’s email address, ignoring capitalisation.
Billow creates a lead for that contact straight away, in the Discovery Call stage with the source Inbound
The booking waits as a pending booking in the Discovery Call column
Billow never creates an account or a contact on its own.

A lead created from a booking is first named after the event type and the invitee, for example “Discovery Call with Jane Doe”. Its notes hold the event type, the date and time of the call, the invitee’s name and email, and every answer from the booking form. Times are shown in your workspace’s timezone.
In the list view, the lead’s source reads Inbound via Calendly or Inbound via Cal.com. On the board, the provider appears next to the contact’s name.
Billow reads each booking once with AI, the same way autofill reads your notes. From the event type and the answers on the booking form, it suggests:
a title for the lead that names the work
an account, either one already in your workspace or a new name, for example taken from the domain of a business email address
The suggestion never sets the stage or the source, and Billow creates no account or contact from it.

For a lead Billow created straight away, the suggested title replaces the name made from the event type and the invitee. The suggested budget fills in while the lead’s budget is still unknown. Neither replaces a name or a budget you changed.

If Billow can’t read a booking, the booking keeps its details without a suggestion. For a pending booking, Billow tries again when you open Create Lead. A lead Billow created straight away keeps the name made from the event type and the invitee.

A booking without a single matching contact waits as a pending booking. On the board, it appears as a card with a dashed border at the top of the Discovery Call column, above every lead. In the list view, it appears as a row at the top of the list, on the first page only. Pending bookings show under the All and Needs action tabs.
A pending booking isn’t a lead yet. You can’t drag it to another stage, and it doesn’t count toward the tab counts.
The suggested title, or the event type until there is one
The invitee’s name, with the provider next to it (via Calendly or via Cal.com)
The date of the call, with a Cancelled badge if the invitee cancelled

The suggested account and budget appear in italics until you confirm them in the lead form. A field without a value reads Unknown. In the list view, the row shows the same suggestions, the source Inbound via Calendly or Inbound via Cal.com, and the stage Discovery Call.
Click Create Lead on the pending booking.
If a dialog offers to create a new account or contact, click Create & Fill to create them, or Skip to choose them yourself.
Choose the Account and the Person of Contact if they are still empty.

The form opens with the suggested title and budget, the source Inbound, the stage Discovery Call and the booking details in the Notes panel. A suggested account or contact that clearly matches one in your workspace is already chosen. The invitee’s name and email appear under Person of Contact.

Billow creates the account and the contact only when you click Create & Fill, and the lead only when you click Create Lead. If the invitee isn’t a contact yet, you can also choose the account, then choose Create followed by the invitee’s name in Person of Contact.

The pending booking disappears once the lead is saved. If someone else created a lead from the same booking or dismissed it in the meantime, the form shows “This booking already has a lead or was dismissed.” Click Save without the booking to save your lead on its own.
Click the X on the pending booking, in the card’s corner on the board or next to Create Lead in the list.
Billow confirms with “Booking dismissed.”, with an Undo button for ten seconds. Undo brings the pending booking back.
Billow follows a booking after it arrives. Each change adds a line to the lead’s notes, such as “Booking cancelled on Oct 2, 2026: Something came up” or “Booking moved to Oct 9, 2026, 2:00 PM CEST.”
A rescheduled booking that Billow never received, such as one made before you connected the account, arrives as a new booking.
Billow drops a booking, instead of holding it for later, if it arrives while:
your plan doesn’t include the lead pipeline
the workspace is read-only because its subscription has lapsed
Bookings made in those periods don’t appear in Billow later. See Failed payments, cancelling and read-only access.
Click the Disconnect icon next to the account.
New bookings for that account stop creating leads straight away. Leads already created stay as they are, and pending bookings stay where they are. You can disconnect while the workspace is read-only.
A connection runs on the Calendly or Cal.com account of the person who made it.
If they leave the workspace or are removed from it, every account they connected is disconnected.
If they delete their Billow account, every account they connected is disconnected.
If the workspace is deleted, every account is disconnected.
A change of role doesn’t disconnect anything.

/help/two-factor-authentication.title: Securing your account with two-factor authentication ⋅ Billow
/help/two-factor-authentication.description: How to change your password, turn two-factor authentication on or off, use and regenerate recovery codes, and get back in when you lose your authenticator.
h1: Securing your account with two-factor authentication
p: Securing your account with two-factor authentication
How to change your password, turn two-factor authentication on or off, use and regenerate recovery codes, and get back in when you lose your authenticator.

Two-factor authentication asks for a six-digit code from an authenticator app each time you sign in, on top of your password. You manage it, and your password, under Settings → Security, part of your personal settings alongside Profile and Appearance. If you signed up with Google, your account has no Billow password yet. Set one first with Forgot password? on the sign-in page, then use the steps below.

Two-factor authentication is a setting on your Billow account. It applies to every workspace you belong to and has no effect on anyone else’s account. Each person in a shared workspace turns it on separately.
In the Update password card, enter your Current Password.
Enter your new password under New Password and again under Confirm Password.
Billow shows “Password updated successfully.” Your new password needs at least 8 characters.
You need an authenticator app on your phone, such as Google Authenticator, 1Password or Authy.
In the Two-Factor Authentication card, click Enable 2FA.
If Billow asks for your password, enter it and click Confirm password, then click Enable 2FA again.
Scan the QR code in the dialog with your authenticator app. If the app cannot scan it, copy the setup key under “or, enter the code manually” with the button beside it and enter the key in the app.
Enter the 6-digit code from your authenticator app.

Two-factor authentication is only on once Billow accepts that code. The card then says “Two-factor authentication is currently enabled.” If you close the dialog before confirming, the setup is discarded and the card shows Enable 2FA again.
Recovery codes let you sign in when you do not have your authenticator app. Once two-factor authentication is on, the card shows a 2FA Recovery Codes section with eight codes.
Click View Recovery Codes to show them, and Hide Recovery Codes to hide them again.
Store them somewhere other than the device that runs your authenticator app, such as a password manager.
Billow issues eight new codes. The previous codes stop working immediately.
Sign in with your email and password, or with Google.
On the next screen, enter the six-digit code from your authenticator app.
To use a recovery code instead, click “login using a recovery code” below the field and enter one of your codes.
Click Disable 2FA at the bottom of the Two-Factor Authentication card.
The dialog asks you to confirm:
Disable Two-Factor Authentication Are you sure you want to disable two-factor authentication? This will make your account less secure.
Turning it off deletes your authenticator setup and your recovery codes. If you turn it on again, you get a new QR code, a new setup key and eight new recovery codes.
Sign in with a recovery code.
Go to Settings → Security and turn off two-factor authentication.
Turn it on again and scan the new QR code with your new device.

If you have neither your authenticator app nor a recovery code, you cannot get back into your account from inside Billow. Owners and admins cannot reset another person’s two-factor authentication. Contact support.

/help/filtering-and-sorting.title: Filtering and sorting lists ⋅ Billow
/help/filtering-and-sorting.description: How to filter and sort the invoices, accounts and contacts lists, how filters combine, how to share a filtered view, and which filters each list offers.
p: How to filter and sort the invoices, accounts and contacts lists, how filters combine, how to share a filtered view, and which filters each list offers.

The invoices, accounts and contacts lists share the same controls: tabs, a Filter button and sortable column headers. The leads page has its own tabs and views, described in Tracking leads in your pipeline.
Open the list and choose a tab.
Click Filter next to the tabs.
Point to a field, such as Account or Amount.
The list updates straight away, and the filter appears as a chip above the list.
How you pick values depends on the field:
Type to search, then tick any number of options. Account, Project and Contact use this type.
Pick This month, Last month, This quarter, This year or Last year. Or pick Custom range and choose the first and last day in the calendar.
Enter a Min, a Max or both, then click Apply.
Date presets follow your workspace’s timezone. This month starts on the first of the month in that timezone.
A row has to match every active field.
Within one field, a row has to match at least one of the ticked options.
Some fields have an extra option at the end of the list for rows with no value. On invoices, Project and Contact offer None. On accounts, Industry offers Unknown. On contacts, Role offers Unknown.
Each active filter shows as a chip above the list, with the values it holds.
To change a filter, click its chip and adjust the values.
To add another filter, click the + button after the chips.
To remove one filter, click the × on its chip.
To remove all filters, click Clear.
The counts on the tabs follow the active filters. If nothing matches, the list shows a message such as “No invoices match these filters.” with a Clear filters link.
Click a column header to sort by that column in ascending order.
Click it again to sort in descending order.
Click it a third time to return to the default order.
An arrow next to the header shows the direction. You can sort by one column at a time.
Healthy and Risky first, then Inactive. Within each group, accounts with overdue invoices come first.
The tab, the filters and the sort are part of the page address. Reloading the page keeps them, and you can bookmark the address or send it to a team member.
Every change to the tab, a filter or the sort takes the list back to its first page.
If you switch tabs, Billow drops any filter or sort the new tab doesn’t offer.
You can sort by Invoice, Account, Project, Type, Amount, Due and Status. On the Paid tab, the Paid column replaces Due, and on the Refunded tab the Refunded column.
Overdue means the due date has passed. Awaiting payment means it hasn’t.
The Drafts section below the Unpaid list follows the same filters and sort. If you set a Stage filter, the Drafts section is hidden, since a draft has nothing due yet.
Healthy, Risky, Inactive, Overdue invoices, Open invoices, Active projects
Every tab. Churned offers only the last three.
The industries your accounts use, plus Unknown
Healthy, Risky and Inactive are the account health labels. Overdue invoices, Open invoices and Active projects match an account with at least one of each.
You can sort by Account, Industry, LTV, APV, Pipeline Value, RS, Added on and Status.
The roles your contacts use, plus Unknown
A contact is Active if they are on a project that is Offer Pending or Active, or on an invoice that isn’t paid or refunded yet, drafts included. Every other contact is Inactive.
You can sort by Name, Account, Role and Added on.

/help/creating-and-sending-an-invoice.title: Creating and sending an invoice ⋅ Billow
/help/creating-and-sending-an-invoice.description: How to create an invoice, send it by email or share its link, what sending changes, how to correct a sent invoice, and what each field in the invoice form does.
h2: Where you can start an invoice
Hide deliverable prices from your client
h3: What your client sees when you send an invoice
p: How to create an invoice, send it by email or share its link, what sending changes, how to correct a sent invoice, and what each field in the invoice form does.
You create every invoice as a draft, which only people in your workspace can see. When you send it, Billow gives it a number, creates a link for your client, and locks it against edits.
Go to Invoices and click Create Invoice.
Choose the Account you are billing.
Optionally choose a Project and a Person of Contact.
Set the invoice date under Issued on, and choose when it is Due.
Choose a Payment Method. For Bank Transfer, also choose a Bank Account.
Add your line items under Deliverables.
Click Create Invoice at the bottom of the form.
Billow confirms with “Invoice draft created.” and opens the invoice page. The draft has no number and no public link yet.
Click Send Invoice at the top of the page. Draft rows in the invoice list have the same button.
If your client’s address or your company address is missing, add it and click Save & Continue. See Missing addresses below.
Read the warning and click Continue.
Enter your client’s email address under Send via email.
Billow confirms with “Invoice sent successfully”. The warning in step 4 reads:
Send Invoice This will mark the invoice as pending and you will no longer be able to edit it.
If the invoice has a contact with an email address, that address appears under the email field. Click it to fill it in.

You can send the invoice link through your own channels instead of an email from Billow. Copying the link of a draft sends it, the same as emailing it: the invoice gets its number, moves to Pending and is locked.
Click Copy Public Link at the top of the page, or choose it from the invoice’s … menu in the invoice list.
If an address is missing, add it and click Save & Continue.
Click Continue in the Share Invoice dialog.

Billow copies the link to your clipboard and confirms with “Public link copied to clipboard”. On an invoice you have already sent, Copy Public Link copies the existing link straight away. See What your client sees when you send an invoice.
An invoice can only go out once both your client’s account and your workspace have an address. Billow checks this when you send, and asks for whatever is missing in one dialog.
Who can add it in the dialog
If your company address is missing and you are not an owner or admin, you cannot continue, even if you add your client’s address. When only your company address is missing, the dialog tells you:
Workspace address required A workspace admin needs to add your company’s address before sending this invoice.
When both addresses are missing, the dialog is titled Add details to send. Ask an owner or admin to add the address under Settings → General, then send the invoice again.
In two situations, Send Invoice and Copy Public Link are disabled on the invoice page. Hover over either button to see the reason.
The invoice has no payment method
The project has a deposit invoice that is not paid yet
“The deposit invoice for this project must be paid first.”
A draft without a payment method also shows “This invoice needs a payment method before it can be sent.” with an Add Payment Method button that opens the form.
If your subscription has lapsed, Send Invoice is disabled until the owner resubscribes. See Failed payments, cancelling and read-only access.
Assigns the invoice number, for example INV-2026-0001.
Moves the invoice to Pending and locks it.
Keeps your client’s details, your company details and the bank account as they were when you sent it. Changing them later doesn’t change a sent invoice.
Shows your current logo, even if you change it after sending.
For emails, sends your client a message with the invoice number and the link.
The email goes out under your workspace’s legal name, whoever on your team sends it.
A sent invoice cannot be edited or put back to draft. You can still mark it paid, resend it, send a reminder and refund it. See Getting paid and Refunding an invoice.

To correct a sent invoice, you replace it with a corrected copy and delete the original. Only owners and admins can delete the original. An invoice paid through Stripe cannot be deleted, so it stays in your list next to its replacement.
A deposit invoice cannot be duplicated, so this doesn’t work for one. For an invoice on a completed project, reopen the project first.
Open the … menu at the top right of the page and choose Duplicate.
In the new draft, open the … menu and choose Edit.
Fix the details and click Save Changes.
Let your client know that the original invoice is void. Its number stays reserved and is never reused.
Open the … menu at the top right of the page and choose Edit.
Make your changes and click Save Changes.
You can only edit drafts. Once an invoice is sent, it is locked.
Create Invoice opens the same form from several places. Depending on where you start, some fields are already filled in.
The Invoices page, the quick-create menu, or Create new invoice in the command menu
A project’s page, from the Invoices card or the banner shown while an active project has no invoices
The project, its account and main contact, and for a project with an offer, the offer’s line items, currency and tax
Links the invoice to one of the account’s active projects
Regular Invoice or Deposit Invoice. See Invoices on a project
Heads the invoice your client sees. If you leave it empty, the invoice is headed “Invoice”
A contact at the selected account
The invoice date. Defaults to today
Immediately, 15 days or 30 days from the invoice date. Defaults to 30 days. Immediately means due on receipt
Bank Transfer or Card Payment (Stripe). An invoice has exactly one
The account your client pays into. Defaults to your primary account
Locked when the project has an offer
The tax rate. Locked when the project has an offer
At least one line item, each with a price above zero
Up to 5,000 characters, shown below the line items
You can create a new account or contact without leaving the form. Open the Account or Person of Contact field and choose Create new account or Create new contact at the bottom of the list.
Each deliverable has a title, an optional description and a price. The price works in one of two modes:
Fixed: one price for the whole line.
Quantity: a rate multiplied by a number of units.
Add a line with the plus button below the list, and drag lines to reorder them.

Your client sees the price of each line on the invoice page and in the PDF. If you turn on Hide deliverable prices, they see the lines without their prices, and only the subtotal, taxes and total carry amounts.
Click the settings button next to the Deliverables heading.

The setting is saved with the invoice and changes no amounts. The PDF leaves out its Qty, Rate and Amount columns, and a card payment through Stripe shows one line for the amount due instead of one per deliverable. The invoice form and the invoice page in Billow keep showing every price, with “Deliverable prices are hidden from the client. They see the totals only.” below the totals.

A new invoice for a project with an offer starts with the offer’s setting. Any other new invoice starts with Hide deliverable prices in Settings → Accounting. Once the invoice is sent, the setting can’t change.
Each invoice carries one payment method.

Bank Transfer needs a bank account in your workspace. Choose one under Bank Account, or click Add new to create one. If you have none yet, click Set up now in the alert to add one in Settings → Accounting.
Card Payment (Stripe) needs a connected and verified Stripe account. Stripe charges its own fees for card payments.

If you choose a method your workspace hasn’t set up, a red alert appears with a Set up now link. If the bank account is held in a different currency from the invoice, Billow warns you that your bank may charge conversion fees. It does not stop you from saving.
The form fills in your default currency, tax rate and primary bank account from Settings → Accounting. Changing them on an invoice affects that invoice only.
Payment Method defaults to Bank Transfer when your workspace has a bank account. Without one, it defaults to Card Payment (Stripe) if Stripe is connected.
With advanced tax mode on, the form shows Tax Label, Tax Rate (%), Second Tax Label and Second Tax Rate (%) in place of Value Added Tax, filled in the same way.

The Project field only lists the account’s active projects. Any other project, including a completed one, is rejected with “Only active projects can be invoiced. Reopen a completed project to invoice it again.”
You set them on the invoice
A simple project, which has no offer
Taken from the offer and locked
Locked fields show the hint “Locked while an offer-backed project is attached”.

If the project’s offer has been accepted with a deposit, and the project has no deposit invoice other than a refunded one, the form shows Invoice Type with Regular Invoice and Deposit Invoice. Regular Invoice is selected by default. See Deposits and automatic invoices.
What is on the invoice page your client opens, how they pay by card or bank transfer, and how long the link keeps working.

/help/simple-projects.title: Simple projects ⋅ Billow
/help/simple-projects.description: How to create a project without an offer, the statuses it uses, how invoicing and plan limits apply, how to delete it, and how to turn it into an offer later.
h2: Turn a simple project into an offer
p: How to create a project without an offer, the statuses it uses, how invoicing and plan limits apply, how to delete it, and how to turn it into an offer later.
A simple project is a project without an offer. It keeps your invoices for a piece of work together, and nothing is sent to your client.
Click New Project on the Projects page, or choose Create Project from the + menu.
Enter the project name and choose the account.
Optionally choose a Person of Contact and write a summary.
The project opens and starts Active.
The client the work is for.
Your main contact at the account.
An internal note. Your client never sees it.
Converting a qualified lead offers the same choice between Project with offer and Simple project. See Turning a lead into a project.
A simple project starts Active. From there you can complete it or cancel it, and either one can be reopened to Active.
Draft, Offer Pending and Rejected only apply to a project with an offer, so a simple project never uses them. See Projects and their statuses.
You invoice a simple project like any other project, while it is Active. Billow does not draft any invoices for you, so you create each one yourself.
There is no offer to take tax settings or a currency from. Each invoice starts from your workspace defaults and stays editable, the same as an invoice with no project. See Taxes on your documents.
You can edit a simple project’s name, account, contact and summary at any status.
Once the project has an invoice, including one you have deleted, you can no longer change its account. The contact stays changeable. See Projects and their statuses.
A simple project takes one of your plan’s active project slots as soon as you create it, because it starts Active. Completing or cancelling it frees the slot. See Plans and limits.
You can add an offer to an Active simple project that has no invoices.
Click Turn into offer in the Project Summary card on the overview.
Fill in the essentials step of the offer wizard.
Click Create Offer in the dialog to confirm.
Nothing changes until you confirm. The dialog explains what happens:

Turn this project into an offer? Saving this step creates an offer and moves the project from Active to Draft. It becomes Active again once your client accepts the offer. The offer cannot be removed later.
From then on, the project behaves like any other project with an offer. See Building and sending an offer.
If the project has an invoice, Turn into offer is disabled with “This project has invoices. Delete them first to turn it into an offer, or start a new project.”
Only workspace owners and admins can delete a simple project. It can be deleted at any status, as long as it has no live invoices.
Invoices you have deleted do not block the delete.
To delete it, open the project, click Delete Project at the bottom of the page and confirm with Delete.
The statuses a project moves through, what causes each change, how to cancel or delete a project, what you can still edit, and how projects count toward your plan.

/help/resend-offer-code.title: Resending an offer to your client ⋅ Billow
/help/resend-offer-code.description: How to resend an offer that is waiting for your client, who receives a new verification code, what happens to earlier codes, and what stays the same.
h1: Resending an offer to your client
p: Resending an offer to your client
How to resend an offer that is waiting for your client, who receives a new verification code, what happens to earlier codes, and what stays the same.

You can resend an offer that is already with your client, for example when they can’t find the email or when someone else at their company needs to accept it. Resending sends the same link with a new verification code. The offer itself does not change.
You can resend while the project is Offer Pending and the offer has not expired.
Click Resend Offer at the top of the page.
Check the Email address. It is filled in with your main contact’s email.
Change the address if the code should go to someone else.
Billow shows “A new code has been sent.” The resend also appears in the project’s activity feed.
The email contains the same link as before and a new code. If you resend to the same address, the new code replaces the one sent earlier, which no longer works.
Resend Offer sits in the same place as Send Offer. While the project is Draft the button reads Send Offer. While it is Offer Pending it reads Resend Offer. In other statuses it isn’t shown.
The address you already sent the offer to
That person gets a new code. Their old code stops working immediately.
That person gets their own code. Codes you sent earlier keep working.

Anyone with the link can open the offer. The code is only needed to accept or reject it. Sending to a second address gives another person at the account their own code, for example someone who has to sign the offer.
The first person to accept or reject closes the offer for everyone. The other codes then stop working.
Once the Offer Valid Until date has passed, the project shows as Expired and the Resend Offer button is disabled:
This offer expired. Edit the project to withdraw it to draft, adjust the validity date, then send it again.
Withdrawing the offer to Draft makes the current link stop working. When you send it again, your client gets a new link and a new code. See Projects and their statuses.
Resending only changes the code. The link and the project’s status stay the same, and your client can keep using the link they already have.
The statuses a project moves through, what causes each change, how to cancel or delete a project, what you can still edit, and how projects count toward your plan.

/help/connecting-an-ai-assistant.title: Connecting an AI assistant ⋅ Billow
/help/connecting-an-ai-assistant.description: How to connect Claude, Claude Code, ChatGPT or Codex to your workspace, what a connected assistant can and cannot change, and how to disconnect or reconnect it.
p: How to connect Claude, Claude Code, ChatGPT or Codex to your workspace, what a connected assistant can and cannot change, and how to disconnect or reconnect it.

You can connect an AI assistant such as Claude, ChatGPT or Codex to your workspace through Billow’s MCP server. MCP (Model Context Protocol) is how assistants talk to other tools. A connected assistant can look up open invoices, draft an invoice or add a lead from a chat. Only owners and admins can connect an assistant.
Click the address under Server URL to copy it.
Every assistant uses the same address:
The URL is the same for every workspace. The workspace an assistant reaches is the one you choose when you authorize it.
The MCP tab only appears for owners and admins.
Name it Billow and paste the server URL.
Sign in to Billow and authorize the connection.
Run this command in a terminal:
In a Claude Code session, run /mcp and follow the sign-in link.
In ChatGPT, open Settings → Plugins, then choose Add → Add MCP server.
Name it Billow and set Type to Streamable HTTP.
Paste the server URL. Leave the token and header fields empty.
When prompted, sign in to Billow and authorize the connection.
Run these two commands in a terminal:
The second command opens the Billow sign-in page. Sign in and authorize the connection.
In a Codex session, /mcp lists Billow as connected.
Signing in from an assistant opens a Billow page titled Connect, followed by the assistant’s name.
If you are an owner or admin of more than one workspace, choose one under Workspace. If you are an owner or admin of only one, the page names it instead.
The page describes what the assistant gets:
Connect Claude Claude will be able to read your accounts, projects, offers and invoices, and to create accounts, leads, projects, offers and draft invoices. It acts as you, in one workspace only.

The connection is bound to the workspace you chose and cannot reach any other. Each assistant connects to one workspace at a time. If you authorize it again and choose a different workspace, the connection moves there and replaces the old one. Cancel sends you back to the assistant without connecting.
If you are not an owner or admin of any workspace, the page says “None of your workspaces can be connected to an AI assistant. Access is limited to workspace owners and admins.”
An assistant acts as you, inside one workspace, and sees what your role lets you see.

An assistant follows the same rules you do: it can only edit offers and invoices while they are drafts, it can’t change what an accepted offer locked, and projects it creates count toward your plan’s active-project limit.
Marks an invoice paid or refunds anything
Converts a lead into a project
Attaches an offer to an existing simple project
Creates an offer on its own

An invoice an assistant creates is a new Billow draft: it gets Billow’s INV- numbering when sent and is not marked Paid. To bring in invoices you already issued in another tool, use Settings → Imports, as described in Importing past invoices. Imported invoices are recorded as Paid, so import only invoices your clients have already paid.

Each connection appears as a card under Settings → MCP. The card shows the assistant’s name, its status, and when it was last used, or when it was connected if it hasn’t been used yet. Connections are personal: you see your own, and other owners and admins see theirs.
The assistant can reach the workspace
The assistant has to sign in again before it can be used
A connection expires after 90 days without use.
Click Disconnect on the assistant’s card.
The assistant loses access to the workspace immediately. It keeps its entry for Billow, so to connect it again later, sign in from the assistant.
Click Reconnect on the expired card.
Click Reconnect in the dialog. Billow removes the expired connection.
In the assistant, add Billow again with the server URL, then sign in and authorize the connection.
Connections belong to the person who made them and depend on that person’s role.
If you leave the workspace or are removed from it, all your connections to it are removed.
If your role changes from owner or admin to Member, your connections are removed.
If the workspace is deleted, every connection to it is removed.
Once a connection is removed, the assistant’s next request is refused with “This assistant is no longer connected to Billow. Reconnect it from your assistant to keep using it.”
Your plan and subscription apply to an assistant the same way they apply in Billow.

If the workspace becomes read-only because its subscription has lapsed, an assistant can still read it but cannot change anything. It is refused with “Your subscription has lapsed. Resubscribe to make changes.” See Failed payments, cancelling and read-only access.
You can still disconnect an assistant while the workspace is read-only.
If the workspace has no subscription at all, an assistant is refused with “This workspace has no Billow subscription. Choose a plan in Billow to continue.”
If your plan does not include the lead pipeline, an assistant cannot create or update leads. See Plans and limits.
How to set your default currency, tax rate, deposit percentage and business targets, and what each default changes.

/help/completing-projects.title: Completing and reopening a project ⋅ Billow
/help/completing-projects.description: How to complete a finished project, what completing changes, how to reopen a completed or cancelled project, and how Completed differs from Cancelled and Rejected.
p: How to complete a finished project, what completing changes, how to reopen a completed or cancelled project, and how Completed differs from Cancelled and Rejected.
A project stays Active until you close it. Completing a project marks the work as finished and frees its slot in your plan.
You can complete a project that is Active and has no draft invoices.
Click Complete Project at the bottom of the page.
Click Complete Project in the dialog to confirm.
Billow shows “Project completed.” and the status changes to Completed.
If the project has draft invoices, the Complete Project button is disabled:
This project has draft invoices. Send or delete them before completing it.
The project no longer counts toward your plan’s active project limit.
You can no longer create invoices on the project. To invoice again, for example for a late expense, reopen the project first.
The offer, the contract, the activity history and every invoice stay as they were. The offer was already locked when your client accepted it.
You can reopen a project that is Completed or Cancelled.
Click Reopen Project at the bottom of the page.
Billow shows “Project reopened.” There is no confirmation dialog.
Cancelled, after your client accepted the offer
Cancelled, while the offer was waiting for your client
A reopened project counts toward your plan’s active project limit again. If you are already at the limit, reopening is refused:
You’ve reached your plan’s limit of x active projects. Complete another project or upgrade your plan to reopen this one.
Complete or cancel another project first, or upgrade your plan.
You stopped the work. See Projects and their statuses.
Your client declined the offer on the share link.
All three free a slot in your plan.
On a simple project, you can complete or cancel the project. Rejected never applies, because there is no offer to decline.
Completing, cancelling and reopening a project each appear in the project’s activity feed, with who did it and when.
The statuses a project moves through, what causes each change, how to cancel or delete a project, what you can still edit, and how projects count toward your plan.

/help/taxes.title: Taxes on your documents ⋅ Billow
/help/taxes.description: How to set a default tax rate, add custom labels and a second tax line, change taxes on a single document, and where your tax registration numbers appear.
h2: How the second tax is calculated
Taxes on a single invoice or offer
p: How to set a default tax rate, add custom labels and a second tax line, change taxes on a single document, and where your tax registration numbers appear.

Tax settings live on Settings → Accounting. A single tax rate needs only Default VAT Percentage (%). Advanced tax mode adds custom labels and a second tax line. Only owners and admins can change these settings.
Enter a rate in Default VAT Percentage (%).
Every new invoice and offer starts from this rate. The rate can be anywhere from 0 to 100, with up to three decimals. Leave the field empty if you don’t charge tax at all.
Tick Advanced tax mode in the Financial Defaults card.
Fill in the defaults that appear below it.
The info icon next to the checkbox explains it:
Shows an editable tax label and an optional second tax line on invoices and offers. Turning this off keeps them on documents that already use them.
Replaces the word VAT on your invoices and offers, for example GST, Sales Tax or IVA. Leave it blank to keep VAT.
Names the second tax line, for example QST.
The rate the second tax line charges.
Each label takes up to 20 characters. A second tax needs both a label and a percentage.
These are defaults for new documents. Changing them never rewrites an invoice or offer you already made.
The second tax line is for places that charge two separate taxes on the same document.
Billow calculates both taxes on the same net amount. The second tax is never applied on top of the first. On $1,000 net at 5% GST and 9.975% QST:
If your client pays by card, each tax reaches Stripe as its own line, so their receipt breaks down the same way your invoice does.
The invoice form and the offer wizard start from your defaults. Changes you make there apply only to the document you’re editing.
Tax Label, Tax Rate (%), Second Tax Label and Second Tax Rate (%)
Leaving a rate empty or at 0% hides that tax line on the final document.
An invoice on a project with an offer takes its currency and taxes from the offer, and you can’t change them on the invoice. The fields show why:
Any other invoice on a project with an offer
“Locked while an offer-backed project is attached”

Unticking Advanced tax mode hides the extra fields for new documents. It doesn’t remove the custom label or second tax from anything already using them. Those documents keep their labels, keep calculating the same way, and still show the advanced fields when you edit them.
The Hide taxes in offers checkbox sits in the same Financial Defaults card. Its info icon reads:
When enabled, offers show only the subtotal. Invoices always include taxes.
The setting has no effect on invoices.
In the Company Settings card, enter your numbers in Tax Registration Numbers, one per line.
The field holds several numbers, up to 500 characters in total. They print under your address in four places:
The contractor details on the public offer page
Contract templates can pull your tax rates in as variables, including Secondary Tax Rate for the second one. See Setting up your contract templates.
How to set your default currency, tax rate, deposit percentage and business targets, and what each default changes.

/help/cockpit.title: Your Cockpit ⋅ Billow
/help/cockpit.description: How to read and adjust the revenue chart, what the stat cards and Open Invoices show, and what a new workspace sees.
h2: When an option is greyed out
p: How to read and adjust the revenue chart, what the stat cards and Open Invoices show, and what a new workspace sees.
Cockpit is your dashboard, the home screen you see when you open Billow. It shows your revenue chart, the stat cards and your open invoices.
The chart shows the revenue your paid invoices brought in during the selected period, counted on the date each one was paid. Invoices in other currencies are converted to your workspace currency.
Above the chart, the total for the period sits next to the percentage change, with a line such as “€1,200 more than previous month” underneath.
Open the period dropdown at the top right of the chart.
The chart reloads for that period. Billow remembers your choice and uses it the next time you open Cockpit. Until you choose one, the chart shows Year to Date.
Week to Date, Last 7 Days, Month to Date, Last 30 Days
Last 180 Days, Year to Date, Last 365 Days, Last 2 Years
Open the ⋮ menu next to the period dropdown.
Choose a view, or turn a line on or off.
Your choices are saved and stay in place the next time you open Cockpit.
Builds revenue up across the period. This is the default view.
Shows each day, week, month or quarter on its own.
Draws your costs as a line, so you can see whether your revenue covers them
Adds your Pending invoices at their due dates, extending the chart forward. An overdue invoice counts from today.
Adds the top of each open lead’s budget range to the projected line
Show break-even needs Monthly Costs set under Settings → Accounting, and isn’t available on the shortest periods.
Show potential (lead volume) is available only when all of these are true:
At least one open lead has a budget.
The period is Last 90 Days or longer.
The stat cards sit next to the chart. They always cover the present, whatever period the chart shows.
How many offers are waiting for your client, and their total. Clicking it opens the Pending tab of your projects list.
How many Pending invoices you have, and their total. Clicking it opens the Unpaid tab of your invoice list.
Revenue paid this calendar month as a percentage of your monthly costs
Revenue paid this calendar year as a percentage of your target
How many accounts are Healthy or Risky. Clicking it opens your accounts. See Account statuses.

Until you set your monthly costs, Costs Covered This Month shows “Click to set monthly costs.” Until you set a target, Yearly Revenue Target shows “Click to set a target.” Either card opens Settings → Accounting, where you fill in Monthly Costs and Yearly Revenue Target.
Open Invoices sits below the chart. It lists every invoice you’ve sent that hasn’t been paid yet, with the nearest due date first.
A new workspace has no revenue to chart. If you’re an admin and the workspace has no invoices yet, Cockpit shows a blurred preview in place of the chart and the stat cards, with this message:
Import Your [year] Business Data Add all your invoices from the current year so Billow can show you all existing metrics and populate your CRM for you.
Click Import now to bring in your existing invoices. Importing fills in your revenue history and creates the accounts behind the invoices. See Importing past invoices.
The building blocks of Billow, how work moves from lead to payment, the two kinds of project, how to use search, and where to start.

/help/trial-and-subscription.title: Your trial and your subscription ⋅ Billow
/help/trial-and-subscription.description: How to start the 14-day trial, when your card is charged, how to update your card and find receipts, and who can manage billing.
h3: Failed payments, cancelling and read-only access
p: How to start the 14-day trial, when your card is charged, how to update your card and find receipts, and who can manage billing.
Billow has no free tier. Every workspace runs on a 14-day trial or a paid plan, and only the workspace owner can manage its subscription.
A new workspace opens on the Choose Your Workspace Plan page until its owner picks a plan.
Choose Pay monthly or Pay yearly with the toggle above the plans.
Click Try [plan] for 14 Days on the plan you want.
Enter your card details on the Stripe checkout page and complete checkout.
Stripe returns you to Billow, which opens your cockpit.
The trial starts when you complete checkout. A card is required, and it is not charged during the trial. The trial covers any plan, with that plan’s limits.
If Billow could not confirm the subscription straight away, you see “Payment received. Your subscription will activate shortly.” Your access opens as soon as Stripe confirms it.
The owner sees “You are on a free trial.” in the sidebar with the time left, and Settings → Plan & Billing shows a Trial Ends in badge.
Your card is charged for the first time when the 14 days are up.
If you cancel before the trial ends, your card is never charged. You keep access until the trial’s end date. See Cancelling.
The trial belongs to the workspace. Each workspace gets one trial, ever.
If a workspace’s subscription lapses and you subscribe again later, there is no second trial. Your card is charged as soon as you subscribe.
Being invited into someone else’s workspace does not use up a trial.
In the Billing Information card, click Manage. If no card or billing email is on file yet, the button reads Manage billing information.
Update your payment method or billing contact on the Stripe page that opens.
Return to Billow from the Stripe page. The Billing Information card shows the new card.
The Stripe page only handles payment details and the billing contact. You change plans and cancel from Settings → Plan & Billing in Billow.
Stripe charges your card and handles the tax on your Billow subscription, so receipts come from Stripe. To find one in your inbox, search for Stripe.
Past invoices are also listed under Billing History on Settings → Plan & Billing. Each row shows the date, status and total, with a Download link to the PDF.
Your settings contain two separate Stripe connections.
The two are independent. Cancelling your Billow subscription does not affect your Stripe Connect account, and disconnecting Stripe Connect does not affect your plan.

Only the workspace owner can see and change the subscription. Admins and members do not see the Plan & Billing tab in Settings. If the workspace needs a plan, they see “Ask your workspace owner to choose a plan to unlock access for everyone.”
How to fix a failed payment, cancel or resume your subscription, resubscribe after it lapses, and what read-only access allows.

/help/team-members-and-roles.title: Inviting people and choosing roles ⋅ Billow
/help/team-members-and-roles.description: How to invite people to your workspace, change their role or remove them, what Owners, Admins and Members can each do, and how seats count toward your plan.
p: How to invite people to your workspace, change their role or remove them, what Owners, Admins and Members can each do, and how seats count toward your plan.
Settings → People lists everyone in your workspace, their roles, and the invitations you have sent. Owners and admins can invite and remove people. Only owners can change someone’s role.
There are three roles. Each role can do everything the role before it can do.
Create and edit accounts, contacts, leads, projects, offers and invoices
Enter the person’s email address under Email.
Choose a role under Role: Admin or Member.
Billow shows “Invitation sent to [email].” and emails the person an invitation link. The invitation appears on the Invitations tab until it is accepted.
Owner is not an invite option. To add a second owner, invite the person as Admin or Member and change their role once they have joined.
Billow refuses the invitation in these cases:
The person is already in the workspace
“This user is already a member of this workspace.”
A pending invitation already exists for that email
“An invitation has already been sent to this email.”
Your plan has no free seats
“Your plan has reached its member limit. Upgrade to invite more people.”
The invitation link is valid for 7 days.
If the person has no Billow account yet, they set a password from the link and verify their email before joining.
If they already have an account, they sign in to join.
Either way, they confirm their name on the Set Up Your Account page and click Join Workspace.
The invitation only works for the email address it was sent to. If they are signed in with a different address, Billow shows an Email Mismatch page.
An expired link shows “This invitation has expired. Please contact the workspace administrator to request a new one.” To let them in, send a new invitation.
Go to Settings → People and open the Invitations tab.
Click the … menu on the invitation’s row.
Click Cancel Invitation in the dialog.
The link stops working immediately. To see expired invitations, turn on Show expired invitations. You can remove those the same way with Remove invitation.

Your plan sets how many people can be in a workspace. Everyone who has joined takes a seat, including you. A pending invitation also takes a seat until it is accepted, cancelled or expires. See Plans and limits.
In the Role column, choose the new role from the person’s dropdown.
Click Change Role in the dialog.
The last owner’s role cannot be changed. To step down as owner, make someone else an owner first.
If you change an owner or admin to Member, any AI assistants they connected are disconnected.
Click the … menu on the person’s row.
The person loses access to the workspace immediately. Everything they created stays where it is. Any AI assistants they connected are disconnected.
You cannot remove yourself. To leave, use Leave Workspace instead.
Owners cannot be removed from the People page. Change their role first.
Click Leave Workspace under Danger Zone.
You lose access to the workspace and need a new invitation to rejoin. Owners see Delete Workspace here instead of Leave Workspace.
One Billow account can belong to several workspaces. You switch between them from the sidebar.
You cannot create a second workspace. A workspace is created once, when you sign up. Any other workspace you belong to is one you were invited to.
How to set your default currency, tax rate, deposit percentage and business targets, and what each default changes.

/help/setting-up-your-workspace.title: Setting up your workspace ⋅ Billow
/help/setting-up-your-workspace.description: How to sign up, verify your email, create your workspace and pick a plan, then complete the setup checklist on your Cockpit.
p: How to sign up, verify your email, create your workspace and pick a plan, then complete the setup checklist on your Cockpit.

You sign up with an email and a password, or with your Google account. Three short steps follow before you reach your workspace: verifying your email, telling Billow about your company, and picking a plan.
On the sign-up page, click Sign up with Google, or enter your email and a password and click Get started for free.
If you sign up with Google, your email is already verified, and you go straight to your company details.
Billow emails you a link. Click it to verify your address.
If the email doesn’t arrive, check your spam folder, or click Resend email on the “Verify your email” page to get a new link.
The “Set up Your Billow Workspace” form asks for these details:
What’s your role within the company?
How many clients do you work with per year?
Click Continue to create your workspace.
Your country sets your starting default currency. You can change it under Settings → Accounting.
Your company name becomes two names:
Your legal name, which your clients see on offers, invoices and contracts. Emails to your clients are sent under this name too.
Your workspace name, the internal label in your sidebar. Billow adds “Workspace” to the end unless your company name already ends with it.
You can change both later under Settings → General, where you also add your address and tax registration numbers.
Every workspace needs an active plan or trial. After you create your workspace, Billow shows the “Choose Your Workspace Plan” page.
Use the switch to choose Pay monthly or Pay yearly.
Click Try [plan] for 14 Days on the plan you want.
Your 14-day trial starts when you complete checkout. You aren’t charged before the trial ends. See Plans and limits.

When you arrive on your Cockpit, a setup checklist sits in the bottom-right corner. Sign up to Billow is already ticked. Set up your finances is the only other required step. It is complete once you’ve added a bank account or connected Stripe, since that is how an invoice collects money.
Click Set up your finances on the checklist. Billow opens Settings → Accounting.
Under Bank Accounts, click Add Bank Account, or under Card Payments, click Connect with Stripe.
Complete the bank account form or the Stripe setup.
The step shows a checkmark once it is complete. See Adding a bank account and Accepting card payments with Stripe.
The same page holds your default currency, default VAT percentage and default deposit percentage. Setting up your accounting defaults walks through them.
The other steps are optional. Complete them in any order:
Clicking a step takes you to the page where you complete it. Create your first project opens the “What kind of project?” dialog instead.

The checklist disappears once every step is complete. After you’ve set up your finances, you can also hide it early with Skip Onboarding or the × in its corner. Hiding it is permanent for the workspace.
Only the workspace owner sees the checklist. Invited team members never see it.
The building blocks of Billow, how work moves from lead to payment, the two kinds of project, how to use search, and where to start.

/help/stripe-connect.title: Accepting card payments with Stripe ⋅ Billow
/help/stripe-connect.description: How to connect Stripe so clients can pay invoices by card, what each verification status means, how to switch a draft to card payment, and how to disconnect.
h2: Switch a draft to card payment
p: How to connect Stripe so clients can pay invoices by card, what each verification status means, how to switch a draft to card payment, and how to disconnect.

With a Stripe account connected, your invoices can offer card payment. Your client pays by card and the invoice marks itself paid. Any admin can connect or disconnect Stripe. You don’t need to be the owner.
In the Card Payments card, click Connect with Stripe.
On Stripe, sign in to your existing account or create a new one.
Complete the business details Stripe asks for.
Stripe sends you back to Settings → Accounting, and Billow confirms with “Stripe account connected successfully.”
If you cancel on Stripe, Billow shows “Stripe connection was cancelled or failed.”
Stripe verifies your account before it can take payments. The Card Payments card shows where verification stands.
Stripe verified your account and it accepts payments
Stripe is still reviewing your details
Stripe is waiting on information from you
While Stripe reviews your account, the card reads:
Verification in Progress Stripe is reviewing your account details. This is usually quick, and no action is needed from you.
If Stripe needs something from you, the card turns orange:
Action Needed Stripe needs more information before your account can accept payments. Card payments can’t be selected on invoices until this is resolved.
Click Open Stripe Dashboard below that message and finish what Stripe asks for there. Billow picks up the change on its own, and you never need to reconnect.
Once the account is active, the card links to your Stripe Dashboard, where you manage your payout settings.

An invoice’s payment method is either Bank Transfer or Card Payment (Stripe). Until your status is Card Payments Active, you can’t save an invoice with Card Payment (Stripe). If you choose it, the invoice form shows “You first need to connect Stripe to Billow to use Card Payments” with a Set up now button. Bank transfer keeps working in the meantime.

An active Stripe account doesn’t make card payment the default. If you also have a bank account, new invoices start on Bank Transfer and you choose Card Payment (Stripe) per invoice. Without a bank account, new invoices start on Card Payment (Stripe).
Connecting Stripe doesn’t change any invoice you already created. To let your client pay an existing draft by card:
Open the … menu at the top right of the page and choose Edit.
Set Payment Method to Card Payment (Stripe).
Invoices you already sent keep the payment method they were sent with, because a sent invoice can’t be edited.

Stripe’s fees and payout schedule are between you and Stripe. Once your account is active, the Stripe Fees tooltip on the Card Payments card gives the standard rate: “Stripe charges approximately 2.9% + 30¢ per transaction. Fees are deducted automatically from your payouts.”
Billow takes no cut of what your clients pay you and never touches the money. Payouts land in the bank account you gave Stripe.
In the Card Payments card, click Disconnect Stripe.
Click Disconnect Stripe again in the dialog to confirm.
Disconnect Stripe Account Are you sure you want to disconnect your Stripe account? Clients will no longer be able to pay invoices with their card until you reconnect.
Billow confirms with “Stripe account disconnected successfully.”

Disconnect Stripe is disabled while any draft or unpaid invoice uses card payment. The card tells you how many, for example “You have 2 open invoices using Stripe. Remove Stripe as a payment method from these invoices before disconnecting.”
For a draft, edit it and switch Payment Method to Bank Transfer.
A sent invoice can’t be edited. Wait until it is paid, or delete it and send a new one.
How to set your default currency, tax rate, deposit percentage and business targets, and what each default changes.

/help/refunds.title: Refunding an invoice ⋅ Billow
/help/refunds.description: How to refund a paid invoice, how each payment method is handled, and what a refund changes.
h3: What your client sees when you send an invoice
p: How to refund a paid invoice, how each payment method is handled, and what a refund changes.
You can refund any paid invoice from its invoice page. Refunds always cover the full amount, and only owners and admins can issue them.
Open the … menu at the top right of the page.
Choose Refund if the invoice was paid by card, or Mark as refunded if it was paid any other way.
The confirmation dialog shows the amount and describes what happens next. The rest depends on how your client paid.
If your client paid by card through Stripe, Billow asks Stripe to refund the card. The invoice stays Paid until Stripe confirms the refund, then changes to Refunded.
If you have since disconnected Stripe, a card-paid invoice shows Mark as refunded instead. Billow then only updates the record, and you refund the card from your Stripe dashboard.
A refund you issue from your Stripe dashboard has the same effect.
If the invoice was paid by bank transfer, or you marked it paid yourself, Billow does not move any money. Mark as refunded only updates the record, and the invoice changes to Refunded straight away.
Send the money back to your client through your bank. The dialog reminds you:
Send the [amount] back yourself Billow only automates refunds for invoices paid through Stripe. Transfer the money back to your client through your bank.
Your client’s bank can reverse a card payment through a dispute, without any action from you. Billow records the dispute in the invoice’s activity feed, followed by its outcome.
Changes to Refunded, the same as an issued refund
Refunded is a final status. The invoice cannot go back to Paid. To charge your client again, create a new invoice.
Refunded invoices no longer count toward the revenue figures on your dashboard.
Refunding a deposit invoice frees the project’s deposit slot. The next invoice you create on that project shows the Invoice Type choice again.
Yes, by an owner or admin
Billow does not email your client about a refund. For card payments, Stripe sends its own refund receipt if receipts are turned on in your Stripe account.

Billow cannot issue partial refunds. You can issue one from your Stripe dashboard, but this is not recommended for now: the invoice stays Paid, and Billow only notes the partial refund in the activity feed.
What is on the invoice page your client opens, how they pay by card or bank transfer, and how long the link keeps working.

/help/plans-and-limits.title: Plans and limits ⋅ Billow
/help/plans-and-limits.description: What each plan costs and includes, how member and active-project limits are counted, and how to upgrade, downgrade or switch between monthly and yearly billing.
h2: When a plan change needs a payment
h3: Failed payments, cancelling and read-only access
p: What each plan costs and includes, how member and active-project limits are counted, and how to upgrade, downgrade or switch between monthly and yearly billing.
Billow has three plans: Solo, Grow and Scale. Each plan sets how many members your workspace can have and how many projects can be active at once. Only the workspace owner can change the plan.
Yearly billing charges ten months for twelve months of access. The plan cards show the yearly price per month, marked “/month billed yearly”. Every plan includes unlimited invoices.
The member limit counts everyone who holds a seat in the workspace:
Your own seat counts. Solo has one seat, so you cannot invite anyone on Solo.
A pending invitation holds a seat until someone accepts it or it expires after 7 days.
Cancelling a pending invitation frees its seat straight away.
If every seat is taken, inviting someone fails with “Your plan has reached its member limit. Upgrade to invite more people.” See Team members and roles.
A project uses one of your plan’s active-project slots while its status is Draft, Offer Pending or Active. Rejected, Cancelled and Completed projects do not count.
Simple projects start as Active, so they use a slot as soon as you create them.
When every slot is in use, you cannot create a project, convert a lead into a project or reopen a completed or cancelled project. Billow shows, for example:
You’ve reached your plan’s limit of 10 active projects. Complete a project or upgrade your plan to start a new one.
To free a slot, do one of the following:
Delete a Draft or Offer Pending project, or a simple project without invoices. Only owners and admins can delete projects, and a project with invoices cannot be deleted.
Upgrade to a plan with more active projects.

The lead pipeline is included on Grow and Scale. On Solo, you can view existing leads but cannot create, edit, move or delete them, and the leads page shows “Leads aren’t included in your plan” with an Upgrade button for the owner.
Choose Pay monthly or Pay yearly with the toggle above the plans.
Click Switch to [plan] [interval] on the plan you want.
Check the new plan and the next invoice amount in the dialog.
Click Confirm switch. Billow shows “Switched to [plan].”
If you’re a founding member and choose Pay monthly, the dialog asks “Switch to monthly and forfeit your founder rate?” and the button reads Switch to [plan] monthly anyway.
The upgrade applies immediately, including the higher limits. Stripe adds the prorated difference for the rest of the current period to your next invoice.
Click Downgrade to [plan] [interval] on the plan you want.
The downgrade applies immediately. Stripe credits the unused time on your current plan to your next invoice.
You cannot downgrade while your workspace is over the new plan’s limits. Billow tells you what is over:
Remove members or cancel pending invitations. The message names how many, for example “Remove 2 members before downgrading to the Solo plan.”
Complete or cancel projects until you are within the new plan’s limit. Billow tells you how many.
Set the toggle above the plans to the interval you want.
Click Switch to [interval] billing on your current plan. Billow shows “Switched to [interval] billing.”

The switch applies immediately. There is no confirmation dialog, except for founding members moving from yearly to monthly, who confirm first because the switch gives up the founding rate. Stripe starts a new billing cycle on the new interval and credits the unused time from your current period against it.
If Stripe cannot charge your card when you change plan or interval, Billow tells you which of two things happened:
“Your plan was changed, but the payment could not be completed. Use Manage billing to update your card or confirm the payment.”
The new plan is active. Only the payment is outstanding.
“Your subscription has a payment that needs attention before the plan can change. Use Manage billing to complete it, then try again.”
Your plan did not change. Settle the open payment first, then change the plan again.
In both cases, go to the Billing Information card on Settings → Plan & Billing and click Manage to update your card. See Your trial and your subscription.

While a cancelled subscription is running out, you cannot change the plan or the interval. The switch buttons are disabled. Their tooltip says “Resubscribe to change your plan.” on the other plans and “Resubscribe to change your billing interval.” on your current plan. Resume the subscription first.

Only the workspace owner can change the plan. Admins and members do not see the Plan & Billing tab in Settings. On a plan without leads, the leads page tells them “Ask your workspace owner to upgrade to use leads.”
How to fix a failed payment, cancel or resume your subscription, resubscribe after it lapses, and what read-only access allows.

/help/subscription-payment-issues.title: Failed payments, cancelling and read-only access ⋅ Billow
/help/subscription-payment-issues.description: How to fix a failed payment, cancel or resume your subscription, resubscribe after it lapses, and what read-only access allows.
h1: Failed payments, cancelling and read-only access
p: Failed payments, cancelling and read-only access
How to fix a failed payment, cancel or resume your subscription, resubscribe after it lapses, and what read-only access allows.

Your workspace keeps full access while its subscription is active, even when a payment fails. It becomes read-only only once the subscription has ended. Only the workspace owner can fix payments, cancel or resubscribe.
Lapsed, or cancelled and the period is over

If a payment fails, Stripe retries it on its own schedule. Your workspace keeps full access while Stripe retries. Every member sees a banner titled Update your payment method. The owner’s banner says “Your last payment failed. Update your card to keep your subscription active.”
Click Update payment method in the banner. It opens Settings → Plan & Billing.
In the Billing Information card, click Manage.
Update your card on the Stripe page that opens.
The banner clears once Stripe collects the payment. If the payment is never collected, the subscription lapses and the workspace becomes read-only.
Click Cancel plan below the plans.
Click Cancel anyway in the Cancel subscription? dialog. Billow shows “Your subscription will end on [date].”

The subscription runs to the end of your current period, and you keep full access until then. Settings → Plan & Billing shows a Cancelled per [date] badge. After that date, the workspace becomes read-only.
If you cancel during your trial, your card is never charged, and access ends on the trial’s end date.
If you hold a founding seat, the dialog lists what you give up instead, and the confirm button reads Cancel and give up seat #[number].
You can undo a cancellation until the current period ends.
On your current plan, click (Click to resume).
Billow shows “Your subscription is active again.” After the period ends, resuming is no longer possible. To come back, resubscribe.

A workspace becomes read-only when a failed payment is never collected, or when a cancelled subscription reaches the end of its period. Every member sees a banner titled Your subscription has lapsed, read-only access.
In a read-only workspace, everyone can still:
View all your accounts, projects, offers and invoices.
Change their own profile, password and two-factor settings.
Export all your data as a zip.

You cannot create or edit anything: no new invoices, no project changes, no invitations and no workspace settings changes. The buttons for these actions are disabled. Hovering over one shows “Subscription lapsed. Resubscribe to make changes.” to owners and “Read-only access. Ask your owner to resubscribe.” to everyone else.
Billow does not delete your data when the workspace becomes read-only.
Click Resubscribe in the read-only banner, or Choose a plan to resubscribe on Settings → Plan & Billing.
Choose Pay monthly or Pay yearly with the toggle above the plans.
Click Choose [plan] on the plan you want.
Complete checkout on the Stripe page.
There is no second trial. Your card is charged as soon as you subscribe, and full access returns. See Plans and limits.
Exports stay available for the rest of a cancelled period and afterwards in read-only. If you want your own copy of your data, export it before you cancel.

Only the owner can delete a workspace, and only once the subscription is cancelled. While a subscription is still live, Settings → General shows “Cancel your subscription before deleting this workspace.” and the Delete Workspace button is disabled.
Export anything you want to keep.
Type the workspace name to confirm.
Click Delete Workspace in the dialog. Billow shows “Workspace deleted successfully.”
What each plan costs and includes, how member and active-project limits are counted, and how to upgrade, downgrade or switch between monthly and yearly billing.

/help/create-lead-from-notes.title: Filling in a lead from your notes ⋅ Billow
/help/create-lead-from-notes.description: How to fill in a lead form from your notes, which fields autofill sets, how it matches accounts and contacts, and where your notes are processed.
h1: Filling in a lead from your notes
h2: Fill in a lead from your notes
h3: Turning a lead into a project
p: Filling in a lead from your notes
How to fill in a lead form from your notes, which fields autofill sets, how it matches accounts and contacts, and where your notes are processed.
Autofill reads the notes on a lead and fills in the rest of the lead form from them. The notes can be in any shape: call notes, a forwarded email, bullet points.
Autofill is included on the Grow and Scale plans, along with the rest of the pipeline. See Plans and limits.
Open a new lead with New Lead, or open an existing lead.
Paste or type your notes into the Notes panel.
If Billow can’t match the account or the contact, decide in the dialog whether to create them.
Click Create Lead, or Save changes on an existing lead.

The lead isn’t saved until you click the button in the last step. Accounts and contacts you create in step 4 are saved straight away, even if you never save the lead. Autofill from Notes stays greyed out while the Notes panel is empty.
A project name taken from the notes
An account already in your workspace that matches the company in the notes
A contact already in your workspace that matches the person in the notes
The budget the notes mention, or I don’t know the budget yet if they mention no money
Billow matches the names in your notes against the accounts and contacts you already have. It doesn’t create new records on its own.
Only confident matches fill in automatically. If a name in the notes has no confident match, a dialog offers to create the account, the contact, or both. It pre-fills what it found in the notes:
Click Create & Fill to create the records and put them in the form. Click Skip to leave those fields for you to fill in. Nothing is created until you click Create & Fill.
On an existing lead, Billow shows “Autofill will only fill empty fields.” Autofill never overwrites an answer already in the form:
Project, Account and Person of Contact are filled in only if they are empty.
Source and Stage are never changed.
Budget Range is filled in only if the lead has no budget set.
On a new lead, autofill also leaves alone any Source, Stage or Budget Range you already changed yourself.
Billow runs your notes through a European AI provider (Mistral). Your notes stay in the EU.
If Billow can’t read the notes, you see “Could not analyze notes. Please try again.” The form stays as it was, and you can fill it in by hand.
How to convert a qualified lead into a project, the two kinds of project you can create, what carries over, and what blocks converting.

/help/leads-pipeline.title: Tracking leads in your pipeline ⋅ Billow
/help/leads-pipeline.description: How to add a lead and move it through the six stages, the board and list views, card order and list sorting, follow-up badges, budget ranges, and how leads leave the pipeline.
h2: Mark a lead as unqualified or lost
h3: Turning a lead into a project
p: How to add a lead and move it through the six stages, the board and list views, card order and list sorting, follow-up badges, budget ranges, and how leads leave the pipeline.
A lead is a potential project you haven’t formalised yet. When you qualify a lead and turn it into a project, its account and contact carry over with it.
Leads are included on the Grow and Scale plans. See Plans and limits.
Click New Lead. To start the lead in a particular stage, click the + at the top of that stage’s column on the board instead.
Enter the project name, then choose the Account and the Person of Contact.
Choose the Source and the Stage.
Set the Budget Range, or tick I don’t know the budget yet.
Add any notes in the Notes panel.
If the company or the person isn’t in Billow yet, type the name in Account or Person of Contact and choose Create new account or Create new contact. Billow can also fill in the form from your notes.
The name of the potential project
The company the lead is for
Your contact at that company. Choose the account first.
How the lead reached you: Outbound, Sales Call, Inbound, Referral or Existing
Where the lead is in your pipeline
Anything you want to keep with the lead
The lead came in and you haven’t talked yet
The lead is paused for now
The lead is a good fit and ready to become a project
The lead is not a fit
The first four are the working stages and show up as columns on the board. Unqualified and Lost are end states and live outside the columns.
The leads page has a board view and a list view. Switch between them with the two icons at the top right. The same four tabs sit above both views.
Every lead in the working stages
Leads in Lead Captured, Discovery Call or On Hold
Board columns, narrowed to those three
Leads in both end states, Unqualified and Lost
The list view shows every tab as a table.
A Converted row shows the project’s status in place of a stage badge, plus a View project button.
Drag the lead’s card to another stage column.
The new stage saves straight away.
To change the stage from the lead itself, open the lead, choose a new Stage and click Save changes.

Drag a card up or down within its column to change its place. The order saves straight away and is the same for everyone in your workspace. When you drop a card into another column, it lands where you drop it.

A lead that reaches a column any other way, such as a new lead or a stage change on the lead’s page, shows at the top of its column. Pending bookings from Calendly or Cal.com stay above every lead in Discovery Call.

The list shows the newest leads first. Click a column header to sort by it, click it again to reverse the order, and click it a third time to go back to newest first. Leads without a value in that column stay at the bottom either way. Pending bookings stay at the top of the list.
Open the lead’s … menu on the board or in the list.
Choose Mark as unqualified or Mark as lost.
The lead moves to the Unqualified tab.

On the board, you can also drag the card onto Unqualified or Lost in the bar that appears at the bottom of the board while you drag. Billow confirms with “Marked as unqualified” or “Marked as lost”, with an Undo button for five seconds.
To move the lead back into a working stage later, open it and change the Stage.
A lead that has sat in Lead Captured, Discovery Call or On Hold for two weeks without a stage change gets a red “You should follow up” badge on its card.
The badge appears on the board only. It doesn’t appear in the list view, and Billow doesn’t email you about it.
New leads start with a rough budget range already set. Adjust it, tick I don’t know the budget yet, or leave it.
